sense: a plan, an attempt or a habit: give up

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation: with the accusative, or the infinitive (“stop doing”)
evidence: Cic. Leg. 1.5: teneō quam optābam occāsiōnem neque omittam (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Let go of a plan, a fear, an opportunity; with an infinitive, “stop” (omitte mīrārī, Hor. C. 3.29.11). It also means “pass over, say nothing of” (ut alia omittam) (Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, with the accusative
evidence: Caes. BC 3.103: cōnsilium adeundae Sȳriae (Lewis & Short)
Catull. 76.13: difficile est longum subitō dēpōnere amōrem
terms.comment: Lay down, and so give up: a plan, a hope, a grudge, an office. Its first sense is “put down, set down” (see put), and it also means “deposit, entrust” (Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation: with the ablative (with or without dē, ab) or the infinitive
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 2.28: dē sententiā dēstitistī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Stop trying, back down; for simply stopping, see stop.

phrases.english: drop everything and look after your health

phrases.latin: difficile est longum subitō dēpōnere amōrem
phrases.english: it is hard to give up a long love all at once

phrases.english: I have the chance I wanted and I shan’t let it go

phrases.latin: quō factō nōn modo dēsistunt pugnā, sed etiam conferciunt sē lingentēs
phrases.english: when that is done they not only give up fighting but crowd together, licking one another
